summary: Master grid modernization and smart metering with this 5-day intermediate course. Design AMI, implement ADMS, and build business cases for a resilient energy fu
lede: Grid modernization and smart metering bring advanced meters, distribution automation, and data analytics into more responsive grid operations. For intermediate energy professionals planning or managing these initiatives, the course covers Advanced Metering Infrastructure rollout design, distributed energy resource hosting capacity analysis, and demand response program development.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for intermediate-level professionals in the energy sector who are responsible for designing, implementing, or managing grid modernization and smart metering initiatives. It is ideal for those with 2-5 years of experience who need to transition from legacy system management to smart grid operations. The course is designed for: Utility Engineers: Design and optimize distribution grid components and automation systems. Grid Planning Managers: Develop long-term infrastructure strategies and DER integration plans. Distribution Operations Leads: Manage real-time grid control, fault response, and service restoration. Smart Metering Analysts: Analyze AMI data, manage MDMS, and support dynamic pricing programs. Regulatory Compliance Officers: Ensure grid modernization aligns with performance-based regulation (PBR) and policy mandates. Energy Efficiency Program Managers: Design and implement demand response and energy conservation initiatives. Cybersecurity Specialists: Protect AMI networks and grid control systems from cyber threats and data breaches. Project Managers: Lead grid modernization implementation, manage supply chains, and oversee rollout timelines. Asset Management Leads: Optimize lifecycle costs and extend asset longevity through predictive maintenance. Sustainability Directors: Align grid modernization with corporate ESG goals and renewable energy targets.
modules: Foundations of Grid Modernization and Smart Grid Strategy
Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) and Smart Metering Systems
Grid Automation and Advanced Distribution Management Systems (ADMS)
Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) and Non-Wires Solutions
Demand Response Strategies and Energy Efficiency Programs
Cybersecurity for Smart Grids and AMI Networks
Data Analytics, AI, and Machine Learning for Grid Operations
Grid Economics, Regulatory Frameworks, and Business Case Development
Grid Modernization Project Management and Implementation Roadmaps
Future Trends, Grid Resilience, and Strategic Planning
Strategic Integration and Executive Reporting for Grid Modernization
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Working knowledge of electrical distribution systems and basic utility operations. No coding or programming experience is required. Familiarity with Excel and basic data concepts is beneficial. Preparation: A pre-course reading guide on smart grid standards (IEC 61850, IEEE 2030) will be provided. Participants should bring a laptop for hands-on exercises involving data analysis and simulation tools.
